sections.advice: Yosemite Valley → Olmsted Point is 10 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Olmsted Point → Tenaya Lake is 4 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Tenaya Lake → Tuolumne Meadows is 12 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Tuolumne Meadows → Tioga Pass climbs about 3031 m in 12 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Tioga Pass → Lee Vining drops about 3031 m over 16 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Tioga Road
scenicChapters.narrative: For 19 km this is Tioga Road, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Tioga Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 8 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

scenicChapters.title: Tioga Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 3031 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

tioga-road.story: A one-way ride of 101 km, Yosemite Valley to the finish - roughly 1 h 22 in the saddle. On the way it passes Olmsted Point, Tenaya Lake, Tuolumne Meadows and Tioga Pass. The highest point is about 3,050 m. Tioga Pass is open in summer only - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
